title_guess: GDP vs GNP: territory vs nationals, net factor income from abroad and its three listed parts, and why India's GNP is below its GDP
recurring_cast: NATIONAL INCOME chip with a GDP / GNP / NDP / NNP checklist (ticks as topics are done)
five coloured country_box squares, India's maroon box with an india_map pin on top
people_dots: each dot a person, its colour the person's country
button_panel with RESET, GDP and GNP pills under the boxes
NFIAD hub: india_map in the centre with three numbered arrows (private remittances, interest on external loans, external grants)
sign_badge: green plus / red minus circles that settle on each hub arm and finally fly into the formula
india_map and country_map silhouettes (US map with flag fill; a small neighbour with its flag) joined by labelled money arrows
running_examples: Jassi (Indian in the US) sends ₹5000 home (+), Alberto (foreigner in India) sends ₹2000 out (-): net remittances +₹3000
India pays ₹2000 interest on a World Bank loan (-) and earns ₹1000 interest on a loan to a neighbour (+): net -₹1000
an Infosys employee on a Walmart project is sent to the US, earns dollars and sends savings to an Indian bank account through a money-transfer service

best_moments.why: a RESET / GDP / GNP button panel under the country boxes: pressing GDP leaves only the dots inside India's box (Indians and foreigners), pressing GNP leaves only India's maroon dots wherever they live; the definition becomes a filter switch
countries as coloured boxes and people as coloured dots that drift into other boxes: territory vs nationality without a single word on screen
the red minus badge from the NFIAD hub flies into 'GNP = GDP + NFIAD' and turns the plus into a minus: the net sign changes the formula in front of the learner
Jassi's green arrow into India and Alberto's red arrow out of India carry ₹5000 and ₹2000; '5000 - 2000 = 3000' writes above: inflow, outflow and net in one picture
after each part the NFIAD hub returns and a plus or minus badge settles on that arm: a running scoreboard of signs

weak_moments.why: about 70 s of a brand-name story (Infosys, Walmart, a money-transfer service and a bank, all as real logos) for one idea; BIE cannot reuse logos
about 35 s of a live-action film clip with real actors and no transcribed speech; recap delegated to it
NDP and NNP rows are shown at the start and the end but never spoken

doubtful content to verify: private remittances and external grants are listed as parts of net factor income (standard national accounts count them as transfers, not factor income); the screen acronym is 'NFIAD' where 'NFIA' is usual
a 'UN Development Partnership Fund' card is drawn sending grants to India; that fund is usually described as India-financed for other countries; check before reuse
the screen ends with 'GNP = GDP - NFIAD' while NFIAD is itself the negative number (strictly GDP + NFIA, or GDP minus its size); the speech says 'always lower' after saying 'mostly negative'

segments.teaches: GDP is done, GNP is today's topic; a country is pictured as a box of its people, and people of one country also live in others

segments.notes: 11 change events in 30 s (2.8 to 27.2): one per phrase. No words on the boxes; colour alone carries nationality.
segments.idea: a country's land and a country's people are not the same set

segments.teaches: GDP counts goods and services produced inside India's territory; GNP = GDP + income of Indians abroad - income of foreigners in India; that difference is net factor income from abroad (NFIAD on screen)

GNP button lights blue; boxes refill, then only maroon dots remain, in India's box and a few in every other box
'GNP = GDP + income of Indians abroad', then '- income of foreigners in India' appended
'Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIAD)' over a blue highlight on the abroad-minus-foreigners part

segments.notes: Events 30.0 (reset), 35.4, 36.4-40.0 (GDP press), 40.8 (GNP press), 48.2, 51.0 (filter to maroon), 54.8, 64.6. The filter at 51.0 lands while 'income of Indians abroad' is spoken. Screen acronym NFIAD (usual NFIA).
segments.idea: GDP asks 'made inside India?', GNP asks 'earned by Indians, wherever?'
segments.shown_as: the boxes slide into a control panel; the GDP button is pressed and every box but India's empties, leaving India's mixed crowd; the GNP button is pressed and the view filters to maroon dots only, at home and scattered abroad, while the formula writes on above: plus Indians' income abroad, minus foreigners' income in India, the last part bracketed as NFIAD
